source.title: Theory III: Dynamics and Generalization in Deep Networks.
source.authors: Andrzej Banburski; Q. Liao; B. Miranda; Lorenzo Rosasco; Bob Liang; J. Hidary; T. Poggio

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including the appendix and figure captions.
record.tranche_reason: Figure 2 reports a CIFAR-10 comparison of networks trained on natural labels and randomized labels, including training classification error and held-out behavior.
record.gate_note: Figure 2 reports results in its caption, but the plotted values are not recoverable from the supplied text. The paper also discusses cited prior work; those cited findings are not rows.
record.test_reason: Figure 2 directly compares natural-label and randomized-label training of 3-layer convolutional networks on CIFAR-10. Its caption reports zero training classification error and chance-level test error for the randomized-label network, testing components of V1.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors argue that gradient flow on separable data with exponential-type losses implicitly controls normalized weight complexity and approaches margin-maximizing stationary points. They explicitly acknowledge that their asymptotic generalization analysis does not explain the usual finite-sample overparameterized regime.
record.recipe_differences: Figure 2 compares training and testing cross-entropy for 3-layer convolutional networks on CIFAR-10, including one network trained with randomized labels. The text does not state the optimizer or full training recipe for this experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: Initializations yielded different testing errors; normalizing each weight layer by its Frobenius norm changed the plotted training-versus-testing loss relationship.

fits_no_version.finding: Layerwise Frobenius normalization yields a plotted relationship between training and test cross-entropy across differently initialized networks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Normalized training loss can track test loss across initializations within a fixed convolutional architecture.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 11 perturbs weights after margin convergence and follows changes in support vectors and subsequent convergence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight perturbations can move a fitted network between margin solutions; this experiment does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness against generalization gaps.

record.problems: Figure 2 is the relevant experiment, but its precise plotted values are unavailable in the supplied text. The figure caption states that the networks have zero training classification error and that the randomized-label network has chance-level test error; it does not give the natural-label test error numerically.
record.rows_left_out: No rows were extracted: the figure caption gives qualitative claims but the required baseline and intervention values are figure-only, so the numeric comparison cannot be assigned. Figure 2.

untested.parts: Natural-label held-out classification accuracy far above chance cannot be established from the supplied text: the plotted measure is cross-entropy, and the caption gives no natural-label classification accuracy. Other architectures and ImageNet are untested; the full training recipe is unspecified.

No reported width sweep establishes continuing decreases in test error beyond the width needed for zero training error. The discussion's statement that error does not worsen with additional parameters does not establish this stronger result.
No convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparison.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison.
No batch-size comparison under matched epoch budgets.
No comparison of magnitude-aware sharpness with generalization gaps or competing generalization measures.
No removal and retraining experiment based on example memorization.

record.verdict_notes: Figure 2's qualitative classification results are usable without exact plotted values. Their omission is already declared in rows_left_out, so they are not listed as missing. Neither differing natural-label test errors nor cross-entropy values alone establish V1's far-above-chance classification accuracy.

versions.untested_parts: Tests a 3-layer convolutional network on CIFAR-10, but does not report extractable numeric held-out accuracy or error for natural and randomized labels.

relationships.condition: Randomized-label component; 3-layer convolutional network on CIFAR-10.
relationships.reason: Figure 2's caption explicitly reports zero training classification error and chance-level test error for the randomized-label network. This supports those components only; evidence is textual because no rows were extracted.
relationships.display_finding: The reported zero random-label training error and chance-level test error remain unverified from the available source.
